Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Great Falls MT
259 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

 -  Areas of dense fog continue this morning for the Milk River 
    Valley in Hill and Blaine County.

 - Light showers will affect Southwestern Montana on Saturday.

 - It will be warm (above seasonal averages) and mostly dry
   through Monday with a cooldown and more widespread
   precipitation expected on Tuesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

 - Meteorological Overview: 

The upper ridge axis over the CONUS Central Plains will continue
to propagate eastward with strong southerly flow over Montana
transitioning to Southwesterly flow over the next 12 to 24 hours.
With support from a broad negatively tilted trough extending from
the PNW through Western CONUS, a weak upper-level disturbance 
will perturbate through the flow bringing generally light showery
precipitation over Southwest MT this morning. Due to surface
warming and ABL mixing, WBZ heights will stay around 3000 FT so 
snow will be containted to the mountain ranges. There is a stable 
layer over the Northern regions of the state with weak easterly 
flow keeping low-level fog producing moisture trapped along the 
Milk River Valley until this afternoon when diurnal boundary layer
mixing occurs. 

For Sunday, warm and dry conditions will persist with
Southwesterly flow aloft maintaining warm air advection to keep
temperatures in the 50s and 60s. With the approaching Pacific 
trough, pressure gradient winds will increase over Southwest MT 
with gusts up to 40 mph expected within the valley downslope 
regions Sunday morning into the afternoon. 

Beginning Monday night, the Pacific system will kick a strong 
upper-level shortwave trough out over western CONUS bringing deep
ascending moisture and instability over Montana into Wednesday and
fueling cyclogenesis over the Yellowstone area. This low pressure
system will deepen and move eastward across the Continental Divide
pulling colder Canadian air south into the region and creating
widespread snow across the CWA by Tuesday night. Moisture laden 
Southwesterly flow aloft with cold northerly advection will 
provide healthy snow growth zone profiles over much of the state.
Most likely placement for a weak deformation zone to develop will
be Northwest of the low over Western and Central MT. - Akins

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios: 

The persistence of fog this morning is high for the Havre and
Milk River Valley areas however current REFS guidance is about
40% probability for the fog extending westward to Shelby and Cut
Bank. For the upcoming winter event Tuesday, ensembles are 
signalling a potential weak deformation zone for moderate snowfall
setting up approximately over Helena and Great Falls. ECMWF and 
GFS show similar mesoscale band placement within the broader 
pattern however intensity, exact location, and duration still 
diverge. Most snowfall estimates for lower elevation areas are 1-4
inches over the Monday night to Wednesday timeframe. Next run 
will bring event time within most short- edium range ensemble 
members for higher fidelity scenario creation. - Akins 

&&

.AVIATION...
14/06Z TAF Period 

Main aviation concern through the overnight period is the likely 
redevelopment of low clouds and fog along the Hi-line, primarily  
affecting the KHVR terminal but potentially extending as far west
as KCTB. Probabilities for visibility less than 1/2SM are around 
60% at KHVR and 30% for KCTB. Otherwise, mid-high level cloud-
cover streaming north into the region continues to thicken 
overnight with some very light precipitation developing across 
southwest MT, where some mountain obscuration may be associated. 
A period of thicker mid-level cloud-cover and some light shower 
activity will spread further north/east across central MT 
Saturday with a shift to breezy west winds occurring at most 
terminals by Saturday afternoon. Hoenisch
